title: Start Simple Daily Dua and Dhikr
whyMatters: Dua and dhikr keep your heart connected to Allah even before you know many Arabic words. They are simple ways to remember Allah during stress, gratitude, and ordinary routines.

exactActions.text: Use your own words in dua
subSteps: Ask Allah for guidance, forgiveness, patience, and good company.
Speak in the language you understand best.
Keep it short enough to repeat often.
Start with phrases you can learn accurately from a teacher or reliable guide.
Repeat them after prayer, while walking, or before sleep.
Do not rush into long lists before you know what they mean.

exactActions.text: Use an authentic dua collection carefully
subSteps: Choose collections that cite Quran or hadith sources.
Mark anything unsourced as something to verify before sharing.

obstacles.solution: You can make dua in your own language. Transliteration can help with short dhikr, but meaning and sincerity matter.

obstacles.problem: I found a popular dua online
obstacles.solution: Do not assume every shared image or post is authentic. Use reliable collections and ask a teacher when a source is unclear.

tinyVersion: Ask Allah for guidance in your own words once today.
unlocksNext: Simple remembrance supports prayer, Quran reading, and emotional steadiness.

commonQuestions.problem: Should I memorize many duas right away?
commonQuestions.solution: No. Start with a few reliable duas or remembrances, understand them, and build slowly.
